title: iTutorGroup to Pay $365,000 to Settle EEOC Discriminatory Hiring Suit
supports_claim: EEOC announced a $365,000 settlement and alleged that application software automatically rejected more than 200 qualified U.S. applicants based on sex-specific age thresholds.
limitations: This is a settlement announcement describing EEOC allegations and relief, not an adjudicated technical root-cause finding; no model, code, denominator, or independent audit is public.

title: Navigating Employment Discrimination in AI and Automated Systems: Testimony of Gary D. Friedman
publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission hearing
supports_claim: The witness testimony recounts the reported Amazon prototype and explicitly cautions that the iTutorGroup mechanism may have been rule-based automated screening rather than artificial intelligence.
limitations: Witness testimony is not an EEOC adjudicative finding; its Amazon account relies on external reporting and its legal discussion is U.S.-specific.

title: Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
supports_claim: Reuters reported that an experimental recruiting model trained on resumes from a ten-year period assigned one-to-five-star scores, penalized some women-associated terms, and was abandoned.
limitations: The report relies on unnamed people familiar with the project; no technical artifact, evaluation population, affected-applicant count, or evidence of sole reliance in final decisions is published.

title: Brief of EEOC as Amicus Curiae in Mobley v. Workday, Inc.
supports_claim: EEOC argued that an algorithmic screening vendor can fall within employment-discrimination law when acting for employers and recorded the plaintiff's allegation of more than 100 rejected applications beginning in 2017.
limitations: EEOC expressly took no position on the accuracy of the allegations, model ownership, or operation; the brief is advocacy on statutory coverage, not a merits judgment.

title: Order Granting Preliminary Certification in Mobley v. Workday, Inc.
publisher: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California via GovInfo
supports_claim: The court provisionally certified an age-discrimination collective limited to applicants aged 40 or older whose applications were scored, sorted, ranked, or screened by enabled Workday AI features and denied an employment recommendation.
limitations: Preliminary certification is procedural and does not prove disparate impact, causation, damages, or a uniform customer configuration; the litigation remained unresolved at the evidence snapshot.

title: U.S. EEOC and U.S. Department of Justice Warn against Disability Discrimination
supports_claim: EEOC guidance identifies disability screen-out, lack of reasonable accommodation, and disability-related inquiries as risks when software or AI assesses applicants.
limitations: Technical assistance explains U.S. ADA considerations and promising practices; it is not a finding about the proposed product or a substitute for Vietnam or EU legal analysis.

title: Testimony of Manish Raghavan on the four-fifths rule for algorithmic hiring
publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission hearing
supports_claim: The expert testimony explains prospective subgroup selection-rate testing and warns that the four-fifths rule is a rule of thumb that should be considered with effect size, statistical significance, validity, and biased labels.
limitations: Expert testimony is not binding law or an agency finding; a ratio at or above 0.80 does not prove fairness, job relatedness, or absence of intersectional harm.

title: EU AI Act regulatory framework and implementation timeline
publisher: European Commission Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
supports_claim: The Commission identifies CV-sorting and other employment AI as high-risk and states that Annex III high-risk rules apply from 2 December 2027 under the current timeline.
limitations: The page is implementation guidance rather than a case-specific legal opinion; provider and deployer roles, exceptions, national law, and future amendments require current counsel review.

title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: The official record confirms Vietnam's AI Law, its 1 March 2026 effective date, and the statutory framework that must be applied with implementing instruments before deployment.
limitations: The official instrument must be read in Vietnamese with implementing rules and product facts; this source does not itself provide a signed classification for FairScreen.

title: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP implementing the Law on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: The implementing decree details risk classification and reassessment, including the significance of intended purpose, human oversight, material changes, and deployment context.
limitations: Application of exclusions or obligations is fact-specific and requires review of the authoritative Vietnamese text; recommendation-only labeling cannot substitute for examining actual reliance.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg promulgating Vietnam's high-risk AI system list
supports_claim: The official decision publishes Vietnam's high-risk AI system list and took effect on 15 August 2026, requiring the final recruitment workflow to be matched against the listed scope and conditions.
limitations: The metadata page confirms the instrument and date; classification requires reading the full list, decree, actual human authority, and downstream effect rather than inferring from an industry risk score.

title: Law 91/2025/QH15 on Personal Data Protection
supports_claim: The official record confirms Vietnam's Personal Data Protection Law and its 1 January 2026 effective date, making a documented review necessary for applicant and fairness-audit data processing.
limitations: Exact lawful basis, sensitive-data status, impact assessment, transfer, retention, and data-subject duties depend on the authoritative text, implementing rules, and actual data flow.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports_claim: NIST's official landing page provides AI RMF 1.0 and its Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage resources and records the framework's continuing update work, supporting lifecycle ownership, measurement, monitoring, and response.
limitations: The framework is voluntary, cross-sector, and being revised; it is not a legal classification, certification, or product-specific proof that controls work.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 General Data Protection Regulation
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
supports_claim: The GDPR establishes EU personal-data processing principles, data-subject rights, safeguards for special-category data, and impact-assessment duties relevant to applicant and fairness-audit data; Article 12(3) uses a one-month response period with a conditional extension.
limitations: The regulation does not determine FairScreen's lawful basis, controller or processor roles, local employment-law interaction, or whether a specific audit attribute may be processed; counsel and the Data Protection Officer must assess the final flow.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
supports_claim: WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation whose technology-neutral, testable success criteria define A, AA, and AAA web-content conformance levels and support an auditable candidate-journey accessibility gate.
limitations: WCAG conformance does not by itself make every user journey accessible, prove reasonable accommodation, or establish a Vietnam or EU employment-law duty; assistive-technology testing and legal review remain necessary.

title: Order Denying Motion for Relief from Nondispositive Pretrial Order, Mobley v. Workday, Document 407
publisher: U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California via GovInfo
supports_claim: The July 2026 discovery order confirms the litigation remained active and addresses whether Workday possessed customer applicant data and aggregated statistics.
limitations: The order concerns discovery and data custody; it does not find discrimination, disparate impact, a common model effect, or technical causation.

title: Decree 356/2025/ND-CP implementing the Law on Personal Data Protection
supports_claim: The official record confirms Vietnam's implementing personal-data decree and its 1 January 2026 effective date, requiring the final applicant-data flow and rights process to be mapped to both the law and decree.
limitations: The metadata page does not resolve FairScreen's lawful basis, data roles, sensitive-data treatment, cross-border transfer, or request deadlines; qualified review of the authoritative Vietnamese text is required.

title: Consolidated Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Artificial Intelligence Act
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
supports_claim: The consolidated AI Act provides the governing text for Annex III employment systems, the Article 6(3) exception analysis, provider and deployer roles, human oversight, notices, and conditional explanation duties relevant to prospective live FairScreen use.
limitations: Classification, exceptions, actor roles, national-law interaction, and which duties apply to a frozen workflow remain fact-specific and require counsel; offline shadow research is not equated with live deployment.

title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Digital Omnibus on AI
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
supports_claim: The amending regulation entered into force in July 2026 and establishes the current transition timeline under which the relevant Annex III high-risk rules apply from 2 December 2027.
limitations: The amendment changes timing and selected implementation provisions; it does not remove the need to classify the intended use, analyze Article 6(3), allocate provider and deployer roles, or comply with other applicable law.
